Top News
 
 
 
 
NikolayPeev/iStock via Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street heads into Thanksgiving week bruised after its worst selloff in years, with the Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) down 10% last week and the S&P 500 ( SP500 ) falling 8.6% as the AI trade came under heavy pressure.

 The spotlight will remain on technology, with Dell Technologies ( DELL ) reporting earnings Tuesday. Investors will focus on AI order backlog, AI -server margins, and guidance after a brutal week for semiconductor and infrastructure names.

 Inflation moves back to center stage Wednesday, when the November core PCE price index is expected to rise 3.2% year over year. The report will be the final inflation reading before the Federal Reserve’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. Durable goods, a second estimate of Q3 GDP and the Fed’s Beige Book are also due Wednesday.

 Black Friday will provide the first major read on holiday consumer demand. A CivicScience survey found 40% of shoppers plan to visit stores in person, the highest level since 2014, with Gen Z expected to lead the rebound. U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and the stock market closes at 1 p.m. Friday.

 Other earnings include HP ( HPQ ), Workday ( WDAY ), Best Buy ( BBY ), Dollar Tree ( DLTR ), Deere ( DE ) and Li Auto ( LI ).

Analysis
 
 
 
 Investing Group Spotlight 
 
 
With closed-end fund discounts reaching their widest levels in over two years, the current market environment is presenting both challenges and potential opportunities for income investors. In his latest article, Stanford Chemist examines the widening discounts, identifies sectors offering attractive valuations, and highlights potential opportunities for investors seeking sustainable income and long-term returns.

( Free Full article ) Here’s a brief summary:

Closed-end fund [CEF] discounts have widened significantly, with the median fund trading at a 9.67% discount to NAV as of November 13, 2026, the widest level since April 2024. Nearly 46% of CEFs now trade at discounts exceeding 10%, creating potential opportunities for income investors. Fixed-income and real estate funds have experienced the sharpest declines, largely due to widening discounts rather than deteriorating portfolio values.

Historically, similar periods of steep discounts have been followed by substantial recoveries, although timing remains uncertain. The article highlights opportunities in funds such as STEW , EIC , SWZ , and OXLC , while emphasizing careful selection, diversification, and position sizing. It also discusses rotating into more attractively valued funds and reinvesting distributions to capitalize on market volatility.

The central strategy remains focused on exploiting valuation gaps while maintaining diversified exposure across different interest-rate environments. For patient investors, today’s wide discounts and relatively stable NAVs could offer an attractive starting point for long-term income generation.
